entries.name: Rope Straight-Arm Pulldown
entries.reason: Source-bound draft: staggered feet and slight quiet hinge; both straight arms sweep from overhead/front to thighs through the shoulders, preserving12.5/12 world lengths and zero elbow flexion. One high pulley, two neutral rope grips, full controlled return. Independent technique/native runtime acceptance required.
entries.summary: Sweep straight arms from overhead to the thighs with a quiet hinge.

frames.caption: Stagger the feet, hinge slightly and hold the high-pulley rope up in front with straight arms.
Sweep the straight arms down through the shoulders; keep the torso quiet.
Finish with the rope at the thighs and the elbows still straight.
Keep the shoulders controlled and the arms long at the bottom.
Return overhead along the same shoulder arc without bending the elbows.

entries.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
entries.reason: Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 28 degrees: starting with the hands at shoulder height and a fixed 168-degree soft elbow angle kept constant across every tick, sweeping the bar down in an arc until the hands make painted contact with the thighs, and returning under control while the cable only lengthens on the pull.
entries.summary: Standing with a small braced hinge facing a high cable and the arms extended at shoulder height, keep one soft elbow angle and sweep the attachment down in an arc until the hands reach the thighs, then return under control.

frames.caption: Stand facing a high cable with a small braced hinge and the arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Keeping one soft elbow angle, lead the arc downward from the shoulders.
Pull the attachment down in an arc until your hands reach your thighs.
Return under control along the same arc toward shoulder height.
Finish at shoulder height with the arms long and the torso braced.
